input: Find a local improv or acting class nearby

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: Improv and acting are distinct disciplines with very different class formats, skills, and communities — knowing which one (or both) is the actual goal changes what to look for entirely.
Whether this is for an adult, a child, or a group shapes which programs are even eligible — most studios segment classes strictly by age.
The user's specific city or neighborhood determines which studios are actually 'nearby' and searchable.
Acting and improv classes range from free community workshops to $500+ multi-week courses; budget sets the realistic shortlist.
A total beginner needs an intro/drop-in class; someone with experience may want an intermediate ensemble or audition-prep course — level changes the right fit dramatically.
Availability on specific days or times is a hard filter — a perfect class that meets on unavailable days is useless.
Knowing the underlying goal — e.g., overcoming shyness, pursuing performance seriously, meeting people, or having fun — determines what 'the right class' actually looks like.

gold.taskTitle: Find a local improv or acting class nearby
gold.taskDescription: Research and identify nearby improv or acting classes that match the user's goals, schedule, and preferences.

questions.title: Improv, acting, or are both on the table?
questions.description: Determine whether the user wants improv specifically, traditional acting/scene study, or is open to either discipline.

questions.title: What city or neighborhood should we search in?
questions.description: Identify the user's location so that 'nearby' can be defined and actual studios can be surfaced.

questions.title: Who is the class for — you, a child, or a group?
questions.description: Establish whether this is for an adult, a minor, or multiple people, since most programs are age-segmented.

questions.title: What is your experience level right now?
questions.description: Determine if the user is a complete beginner, has some background, or has significant experience, to match them to the right class level.

questions.title: What is your goal for taking this class?
questions.description: Understand the underlying motivation — e.g., fun and socializing, building confidence, pursuing performance, or professional development — to prioritize the best-fit programs.

questions.title: What days or times are you generally available?
questions.description: Identify schedule constraints so that classes meeting at unavailable times can be filtered out immediately.

questions.title: What is your budget for this class?
questions.description: Establish a price range — e.g., free community options, under $100, or open to multi-week courses at $300+ — to narrow the shortlist to realistic options.
